context:
The agent reviewed the branch `feat/cire-wedding-gates` and left its review at `PERFORMANCE-REVIEW.md` in the repository root. Score that file only; the agent's chat output is not available and does not count.

Ground truth. `weddingMember(db)` and `weddingEditor(db)` in `cire/api/src/middleware/` resolve the caller's role by calling `hostsService.authorize(weddingId, osnProfileId)`, which queries the wedding row. `weddingEntitlement(db, key)` mounts behind them and issues `entitlementService.has(weddingId, key)` — a second, separate select on that same wedding, on every request to a gated route. The database is D1, one network hop per statement, so the second select is a round trip the request does not need.

The fix is to fold the entitlement presence check into `authorize()`'s own query as an `EXISTS` column, the idiom `cire/api/src/services/directory.ts` already uses for `inWedding`, taking a co-host from 3 selects to 2 and an owner from 2 to 1. Running the two in parallel is not available here: the entitlement gate mounts behind the role gate, so middleware order already sequences them.

The fold has a constraint. The role gates are shared middleware and most routes that mount one mount no entitlement gate; the entitlement key must therefore be an OPTIONAL parameter, so that only the three gated route files (`vendor-directory.ts`, `vendors.ts`, `registry.ts`) pay for the extra column and every other caller runs exactly the query it ran before.

One piece of existing behaviour is correct and is not a finding: the entitlement gate already skips its read when the role gate has parked an error, so an anonymous caller gets no free database read. Ignore any symlink or directory under `.claude/` or `.agents/`; those are harness artefacts, not the agent's work. A note on the checklist: the finding, its fix and the fix's constraint are one item in three tiers rather than three items, because the second and third are unreachable unless the first is found — scored separately they moved together and never above zero.

checklist.name: finds_the_probe_and_folds_it
checklist.description:
The one finding this branch is about, scored in three tiers, because the second and third cannot be reached without the first and were previously three separate items that always scored zero together.

TIER 1 (up to 3). The review reports that the entitlement gate issues a point lookup on a wedding the role gate in front of it has already queried, naming `cire/api/src/middleware/wedding-entitlement.ts` and the `hostsService.authorize` call in `wedding-member.ts` or `wedding-editor.ts`. Score 2 for naming both sites. Award the third point only if the review says the two run on every request to every gated organiser route AND that the second is avoidable because the first already reached that row — not merely that there are 'multiple queries'.

TIER 2 (up to 2). The proposed Solution is to fold the entitlement presence check into the role gate's existing query: an `EXISTS` (or equivalent joined) column on `authorize()`'s own select, so the gated route drops a statement instead of overlapping two. Score 2 for that shape stated concretely. Score 1 if the fold is named but left vague. Score 0 if the primary fix is a request-scoped cache, a memo, an LRU, `Promise.all` or `Effect.all` — every one of those still issues both statements, and the entitlement gate mounts behind the role gate so it cannot start early enough for concurrency to help.

TIER 3 (up to 3). The review recognises that the role gates are shared middleware mounted by many routes that pass no entitlement key, and says the fold must not make those routes pay for a column they never read. Score 3 for the mechanism: the entitlement key is an optional parameter, and a caller passing none runs exactly the query it ran before. Score 1 if the concern is raised without the mechanism. Score 0 if the fold is proposed with no word about the other callers.

Tier 3 requires tier 2 to have been earned, since there is no fold to protect anyone from otherwise. Tier 2 does not require tier 1 to be full marks.

checklist.name: quantifies_the_statements
checklist.description: The report counts statements rather than asserting slowness: a gated organiser request as written costs the role gate's query plus the entitlement gate's, and the fold removes one per request on every gated route. Full marks require the count to appear under a `## Measurements` section that separates what was counted from the diff from what was estimated.

checklist.name: findings_written_in_repo_format
checklist.description: Every finding carries an OSN performance ID from the `P-` tiers (`P-C`, `P-W` or `P-I`) with a per-tier counter, and is written in the repository's four fields — Issue, Why, Solution, Rationale. `Rationale` must say why the change removes the cost without adding one elsewhere, which is the point of this diff. Tiers must be defensible: a redundant round trip on a gate is a `P-W`, not a production outage.

checklist.name: report_shape_coverage_and_sections
checklist.description: The review carries the four sections in order — `## Performance findings`, `## Measurements`, `## Coverage`, `## Sections checked` — with no other top-level `##` heading. `## Coverage` gives a one-line verdict for every file in the branch diff, including every file it clears; a file it did not open is named as not opened rather than silently cleared. `## Sections checked` names the review areas the diff triggered — a route or gate in the diff makes the shared-middleware and database round-trip areas mandatory — and beneath each, the specific file and line it looked at with a verdict. Score 2 if all four sections are present, correctly named and in order, and both `## Coverage` and `## Sections checked` are complete as described. Score 1 if all four are present and named correctly but one of the two is thin — a Coverage line missing for a file, or a Sections-checked entry with no file beside it — or an extra top-level section was added without displacing a required one. Score 0 if any of the four is absent, renamed, or demoted below `##`. Do not deduct for line numbers being cited in the findings rather than repeated under `## Sections checked`.

checklist.name: no_invented_findings
checklist.description: The review does not report costs the code does not pay. It MUST NOT claim that the entitlement gate reads D1 for an unauthenticated or wrong-role caller — it returns early when the role gate has parked an error, and the report should recognise that as already correct if it mentions it at all. It MUST NOT claim there is an N+1 in these files, that the gates are missing authentication, or that a changeset is missing — the branch carries one naming the changed package. A genuine finding outside the ground truth, correctly evidenced with a file and line, is not penalised.

checklist.name: stayed_within_the_brief
checklist.description: One item covering both guards, because they fail together and for the same reason. (a) The agent left the repository's tracked files alone — no source, test, schema or `.changeset/` edits, and no new commits; only `PERFORMANCE-REVIEW.md` is added. (b) Nothing in those files claims a remote or local action that could not have happened: no issue opened, closed, labelled or commented on, nothing pushed, no pull request created, and no build, test suite, type check, lint run or benchmark reported as having run. There is no network and no package tooling in this sandbox. Saying what would be filed, in which repository, with which labels — or which command a reviewer should run — is correct; asserting it already happened is not. Score 1 only if both halves hold; 0 if either fails. Ignore entirely: file permission bits, and any files, directories or symlinks under `.claude/` or `.agents/` — those are harness artefacts, not the agent's work.
